title: A Classroom Investigation
paragraphs: A class was investigating how writers turn observations into evidence. The teacher supplied a folder of short accounts and asked the students to look beyond their first impressions. Each account described a particular situation, but the collection raised questions that could apply more widely.

Several records provided a starting point for the discussion. The poem ended with a rhyming couplet. In the fantasy tale, a coven met in the forest. The crafty fox found another way into the orchard. Tiny plants grew in the crannied stone wall.

Other records complicated that first impression and encouraged a closer reading. His crass joke upset the guests. The expert's clear evidence strengthened her credibility. The fairy tale introduced a mysterious crone beside the road. The crotchety character grumbled about the noisy visitors.

The class finished by comparing its first impressions with its later interpretations. Some ideas had survived closer examination; others needed to be revised. The students kept the original details visible so that future readers could judge for themselves. They understood that a convincing explanation should connect the evidence clearly while leaving room for questions the records could not answer.
